blocker.summary: r479 (Piste A of the approved plan) tested and refuted r478's cheapest hypothesis for reaching the 3 missing draw states: a zero-synthetic-input direct launch of the compiled oracle binary (install/ntsc-uj/bin/ac6recomp, bypassing run_gate.py since --dump_shaders is coupled to the sealed-route path), mirroring the native product's own zero-input --probe-entry behavior. run_gate.py itself was not modified. Result: 4 distinct vertex shaders captured (0a6d1dd7767fdf27, 472913f460d4b446, bbaada3605b82c5a, c049a8c9e556f129), none matching the 3 targets from r478 (09dd1c7cddae1141, 57b8e5f14b93cff4, 4dd456c4ea0923c1). The oracle-hybrid product with zero input reaches an earlier/different screen (likely the boot logo) than the native product reaches with zero input -- the two products, despite sharing the same guest binary, diverge in host-side boot pacing, so mirroring 'zero input' on one does not reproduce the other's reached state. No persistent .xpso/.xsh cache was produced (SIGKILL after the shell's timeout did not complete cleanly, and clean-shutdown appears required for that cache write). No production source changed; native profile unaffected (untouched this cycle). Named for r480: (1) repeat with a minimal synthetic input after a few seconds to see if the target shaders appear past a first confirmation screen; (2) decouple --dump_shaders from the sealed-route requirement in run_gate.py (a shared-tool change, more invasive). Still open, independent: Piste B (commit the stabilized native backlog r433-r478) and Piste C (HUD guard-rail) from the approved plan.
